summary: Eastern (Byzantine) liturgical calendar feature — backend + frontend fully verified. 16/16 pytest cases pass against the public URL, covering Nativity/Theophany +13-day shift, Pascha differing between new (Gregorian) and old (Julian) computus in 2026, Great Feasts (Transfiguration, Dormition, Annunciation, Pentecost, Ascension), 400 on invalid month/date, and Roman calendar unchanged. UI: on the Calendar tab (mobile viewport 390x844) — tapping 'Eastern (Byzantine)' reveals New/Old chips; the month grid reloads and the day detail card shows the correct Byzantine feast/season. Verified: NEW Dec 25 2026 → 'Nativity of Christ'; OLD Dec 25 2026 → 'Nativity Fast (Philip's Fast)' with no feast; OLD Jan 7 2027 → 'Nativity of Christ'; OLD Jan 19 2027 → 'Theophany'; NEW Jan 6 2027 → 'Theophany'. Roman toggle restores the Roman grid and hides the New/Old chips. No red screens, no crashes, loading indicator resolves.
critical_code_review_comments: eastern_calendar.py is small, focused and well-commented; feast tables and moveable cycle look correct. JULIAN_OFFSET_DAYS=13 is only valid for 1900-2099 (already documented in the module docstring).
server.py: /api/eastern/* endpoints are public (no auth) — matches /api/liturgical/* behaviour, which is intended for calendar rendering.

calendar.tsx correctly reuses the existing LiturgicalDay renderer for both rites; the New/Old chip row only renders when rite='eastern' (good), and the load() dependency array includes rite + eastCal so refetch happens on every toggle.
seed_data_creation: None — endpoints are stateless and public.
context_for_next_testing_agent: Eastern-calendar toggles (cal-rite-roman/cal-rite-eastern, cal-eastcal-new/cal-eastcal-old) are stable. If regressing, the Playwright script in this iteration navigates by clicking cal-next N times (today=2026-07 → +5 = Dec 2026, +6 = Jan 2027) and asserts on cal-detail-card text.
